content:
The image shows a mango leaf with brown, necrotic tissue concentrated at the tip and spreading downward along the edges. The necrosis is dry, tan-to-brown in color, with irregular margins. The green portion of the leaf appears otherwise relatively healthy with no white powdery coating, no black sooty deposits, and no stem/branch dieback visible.

Key observations:
- Tip necrosis (brown, dead tissue from the leaf tip inward) — classic pattern for Anthracnose on mango
- Dry, irregular brown lesions along the upper portion
- No white powdery patches (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No black sooty coating (rules out Sooty_Mould)
- Only the leaf is shown, no stem dieback (Die_Back typically affects shoots/stems)
